ideas.risks: The strongest route will fail unless exact theorem assumptions (labels/margins/complexity) are met. Risk of mapping mismatch is high, especially around binary outputs and distribution-free runtime. Also high chance no theorem in current form gives true OPT+ε rather than OPT+α+ε.
ideas.summary: Build an explicit theorem-by-theorem compatibility matrix for KMV08, Feldman, and potential-based agnostic boosting: source oracle form, required weak hypothesis output (binary/real/confidence), per-round complexity, and final excess form (OPT+ε vs OPT+α+ε). The first deliverable should be a table with theorem IDs and quantified parameter substitutions.
ideas.title: Complete Route-D oracle compatibility matrix with exact theorem IDs
ideas.why_promising: If existing boosters already imply the target under this exact model, this audit is the shortest path to closure; if not, it gives a precise negative/fence for where extra assumptions are indispensable.

ideas.risks: May be class-specific and too weak to generalize; proving lower bounds under adaptive filters is technically hard and may require bespoke hard distributions that do not separate the atlas-wide edge.
ideas.summary: Construct an explicit quantified (C,D,F) obstruction where OPT_C(D) is small but for every adaptive residual/clipping wrapper in a natural family, after O(poly(1/ε)) rounds either mass(D_t) becomes <1/poly(n,1/ε) or OPT_C(D_t)≥1/2−1/poly(n,1/ε). Include all quantifiers and dependence on β and stopping time.
ideas.title: Explicit adaptive filtering obstruction for invariant route
ideas.why_promising: A single quantified witness would settle a strong negative route or at least fence off entire classes of wrapper-based positive proofs.

ideas.risks: Adaptive dependence and stopping times can invalidate naive concentration bounds; need strong dependence control and finite-sample corrections. Could produce only partial statements.
ideas.summary: Prove (or disprove) a high-confidence, computable per-round estimator of γ_t = 1/2−OPT_C(D_t) from wrapper statistics under adaptive sampling and stopping times, with guarantees polynomially stable in n,1/ε,log(1/δ),1/(1/2−β).
ideas.title: Adaptive γ_t certification under stopping-time dependence
ideas.why_promising: All positive conditional routes currently depend on this; turning it into a theorem would make Route A computationally meaningful.

ideas.risks: May require importing nontrivial SQ-lower-bound machinery and matching constants; could fail if interface mismatch is larger than precision limitation itself.
ideas.summary: Formalize the fixed-solver oracle as an SQ/statistical query primitive with binary 0/1 excess-risk returns (fixed additive β) and derive whether boosting to ε is impossible below certain query precision or tolerance in this interface.
ideas.title: SQ/precision barrier for fixed-β to ε-agnostic amplification
ideas.why_promising: A conditional barrier theorem would explain why adaptive wrapper/boosting efforts fail without extra structure and give a principled negative result.

ideas.risks: May only hold under additional assumptions and not affect the general edge; proving sufficiency for improper learners with restricted outputs may still be difficult.
ideas.summary: Characterize explicit subclasses where the conversion is true: e.g., Tsybakov/Massart margin, bounded condition number, or filter-stability classes where OPT_C(D_t) non-increases (or drops by constant) under the wrapper updates. Provide minimal sufficient assumptions and full complexity dependence.
ideas.title: Conditional subclass theorem under margin/filter-stability
ideas.why_promising: A positive conditional theorem is directly usable for atlas taxonomy and can reveal natural separating assumptions that current blockers avoid.

ideas.risks: Might require nontrivial interface surgery of boosting algorithms; may still leave residual floors. Could be impossible without altering weak oracle contract.
ideas.summary: Design a wrapper that outputs a richer confidence-weighted hypothesis from multiple fixed-slack calls (bagging/ghost samples/debiased disagreement) so each query satisfies stronger weak-learner contracts needed by known theorems while preserving output-agnostic and polynomial constraints.
ideas.title: Confidence-augmentation wrapper for oracle mismatch
ideas.why_promising: Could bypass the strongest interface mismatch without changing the fundamental fixed-slack guarantee, enabling direct use of existing boosting theorems if correctness can be proved.
